description: OpenGeoStat contributors maintain PyGSLIB, a Python module that wraps selected GSLIB geostatistical routines and supports mineral-resource estimation. Its README names interpolation, geostatistics, documentation and a Python package, including Fortran-derived components. Users supply spatial samples, grades and model settings; outputs are estimates or simulated spatial fields over a deposit grid. Geographic coverage follows the sampled mining site. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing for this repository, but users should check terms of separately supplied dependencies. A limitation is that resource estimates depend on sampling quality, variogram choices and geological boundaries; they are not verified ore reserves without further assessment. The software can prepare subsurface inputs for mining and associated transport, power and water infrastructure scenarios. The related catalogue QGIS platform is a separate GIS interface, not a mineral-estimation engine. No drill-hole data, grids or software archive was downloaded.
name: PyGSLIB mineral-resource geostatistics
